Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: DISTANT / BACKGROUND LAYER of a two-plane Europa Universalis V loading illustration. Generate ONE landscape painting, full 16:9 canvas, target 3840x2160.
The three input images are STYLE REFERENCES: original EU5 Florence artist workshop, original EU5 Hanseatic market, original EU5 Zheng He Chinese harbor. Match this exact art direction: richly observed historical narrative painting, coherent ordinary human figures engaged in clearly readable tasks, visible deliberate broad brushwork and modeled color planes, hand-painted faces and fabric, lively but restrained earth reds/blue-gray garments, warm daylight and blue-green atmospheric distance. NOT a photograph, NOT a 3D render, not fantasy concept art, not sepia or desaturated cinema.
SUBJECT: a BUSY PREINDUSTRIAL SALT-WELL WORKS in the Zigong region of Sichuan, China, early seventeenth-century / late Ming inspiration. A believable bustling working settlement among low green Sichuan hills; show the complete production chain in one convincing perspective.
COMPOSITION: wide view from an elevated earthen loading yard looking slightly down into the works. Main iconic weathered timber well hoisting frame at x32%, top safely below y9%, its timber joinery and rope lashings legible, A-frame timber construction with suspended narrow brine bailer tube and real rope aligned over a SMALL well mouth. Moderate historical scale, not a modern drilling tower. At its foot, a large simple wooden winding drum/capstan and a small team of workers visibly coordinating the rope. Behind and around it, a few smaller timber hoisting structures, not an endless forest of towers. On the middle-right, an OPEN-SIDED tiled-roof boiling shed, roof high enough to clearly see three or four shallow wide iron salt pans over brick/stone furnaces. White steam rises naturally from the pans, subtle warm furnace light beneath, workers stir or rake salt using long wooden tools. Hollow bamboo brine pipes run on low wood supports from the well side toward settling vats and the shed: a continuous plausible route, not random disconnected plumbing. Workers carry matched wooden buckets with shoulder poles along a central lane; another small group packs coarse white salt into woven baskets near a timber storeroom. Around 15-22 small to medium figures distributed in distinct task groups, believable scale and limbs, no duplicated poses, no huge crowd soup. A low timber bridge or stream and village houses recede into green hills in the upper distance.
FULL-PLATE REQUIREMENTS: This is a completely painted opaque background that will later receive a SEPARATE transparent foreground with large workers in the lower-right quarter. Paint the whole ground beneath those future workers. Keep x68..98%, y68..100% as a quiet near earthen staging terrace, visually connected to the central lane, with little clutter and NO close-up people yet. Keep major well, pans and task groups above that near foreground and away from screen edges. No foreground close-up silhouettes framing the bottom. Clear depth progression, complete edge-to-edge landscape, no holes or blank mask shapes. Bright pale blue sky occupies roughly upper fifth; steam integrates with the sky without swallowing the architecture. No giant smokestacks, electric machinery, iron oil derricks, rail tracks, modern steel pipes, modern safety clothing, sea salt evaporation flats, text, signs, logos, borders, fake calligraphy or UI.
The image must feel like an actual native EU5 loading painting of productive daily life, not a museum diagram or travel poster. One single painting.
